short: A catastrophic shipwreck that killed the English heir and triggered a succession crisis.
full:
On 25 November 1120, the White Ship sank in the English Channel shortly after departing from Barfleur in Normandy. The vessel struck a submerged rock in the dark and capsized, killing nearly all three hundred people aboard. Among the dead were numerous prominent nobles and, most significantly, William Adelin, the only legitimate son and heir of King Henry I.

The disaster threw the Anglo-Norman succession into turmoil. Having lost his male heir, Henry later forced his barons to swear oaths of allegiance to his daughter, Empress Matilda. When Henry died fifteen years later, the barons refused to accept female rule and instead supported his nephew, Stephen of Blois. The sinking of a single vessel thereby caused the devastating nineteen-year civil war known as the Anarchy.
